coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Mission Bay Commons P12: SFF Soccer and Fitness Court
names: Mission Bay Commons P12: SFF Soccer and Fitness Court
record.summary: Parcel P12, the westernmost of the three west Mission Bay Commons parcels (between Long Bridge St and Merrimac St), holds the SFF Soccer and Fitness Court, as OCII's November 14, 2024 update (PDF p.17 legend) labels its current use. It began as an interim use (OCII's timeline gives 2018 for the P12 pilot), pending the Mission Bay Future Parks Project, which Rec and Park says will renovate parcels P12, P13 and P15 into a permanent park. The permanent park is one project for P12, P13 and P15 together, so the schedule shown here (construction beginning late 2028 and opening early 2030 on Rec and Park's estimated schedule, expected dates that differ by source) is the project's, not specific to this parcel.

notes.accuracy_caveat: The shape is approximate but its outer edge is real. The outer edge is OpenStreetMap way 446183018 (leisure=park, name 'Parklab', community-surveyed). The lines between the three parcels are not surveyed parcel lines: they are drawn at DataSF's official street centerlines for Merrimac St and 4th St, which are roadways across the strip, offset 6.8 m each side (checked on satellite imagery; at Merrimac St the paved crossing is only about 10-11 m wide with the centerline near its east edge, so the line on the P13 side falls about 2-3 m inside the community garden beds, leaving about 70-100 sq m of them out of P13), and the order of the parcels, P12 then P13 then P15 from west to east, is from OCII's November 14, 2024 update (PDF p.17), whose drawing is not to scale. This parcel is the westernmost of the three, from the OSM outline's west end to Merrimac St, about 4,780 sq m. The shape is not clipped to the street layer (street_clip_exempt): clipping a drawn outline against DataSF centerline buffers would cut P12 in two along DataSF's Long Bridge St segment, which crosses the soccer field where imagery shows no roadway, and would trim the north edges of P12 and P15, so the processed shape is the drawn one. This parcel has no Assessor lot of its own: Assessor lot 8710003 (17,562 sq m, active) contains all of this parcel, which is only about 27% of that lot, so the lot is a larger shared lot, not this parcel's own. The interim uses here are as OCII labels them (OCII's legend label "SFF Soccer + Fitness Court"); they are interim pending the Mission Bay Future Parks Project, which is planned to redesign parcels P12, P13 and P15 into a permanent park (expected dates differ by source; see the record page).
notes.digitized_from: OpenStreetMap way 446183018 (leisure=park, name=Parklab) outer edge, cut at DataSF's official centerlines of Merrimac St and 4th St, plus and minus 6.8 m (4th St's roadway is excluded; the Merrimac St line falls about 2-3 m inside P13's community garden beds) into OCII's parcels P12, P13 and P15 (OCII Nov 14, 2024 update, PDF p.17)

record.name: Mission Bay Commons P12: SFF Soccer and Fitness Court

open_questions: No official parcel boundary was found for P12: The outline is the OpenStreetMap park strip named Parklab (way 446183018), cut at Merrimac St along DataSF's street centerline plus 6.8 m; the lines between parcels are drawn from OCII's November 2024 drawing (PDF pp.5 and 17), which is not to scale, not from a survey. This parcel has no Assessor lot of its own: lot 8710003 (17,562 sq m) holds all of P12, but P12 is only about 27% of that lot.

The start of the soccer use is not settled: SFF Soccer's About page says "In 2013, the ground was broken, the turf was laid, the lights went up" and speaks of "The fields at Mission Bay" without naming a parcel, while OCII's slide 9 gives 2018 for the P12 pilot. No source ties the 2013 fields to P12, so no opening date is stated.

The Fitness Court is named only in OCII's legend ("P12 SFF Soccer + Fitness Court"); Rec and Park's page lists "SFF soccer fields" and no fitness court, and no source read says who runs or when it opened.

OCII's drawing places P12 between Long Bridge St and Merrimac St, but DataSF's Long Bridge St centerline crosses the mapped strip under the soccer field, where satellite imagery shows no roadway; the west end of this outline is as OpenStreetMap has it.

The schedule differs between sources and is not resolved: Rec and Park's project page gives "Construction begins, Late 2028" and "Open to the Public, Early 2030" but also says the remaining parks "are anticipated to be complete by 2028", and slide 9 of OCII's November 14, 2024 update reads "Construction (mid-2027 thru 2028)" and "Transfer to SF Rec Park and Park (end of 2028, upon completion)". All of these are expected dates.

The OCII November 2024 deck's timeline (slide 9) is an image with no text layer; it was read on 2026-10-12 from a rendering of the slide. It gives "Construction (mid-2027 thru 2028)" and "Transfer to SF Rec Park and Park (end of 2028, upon completion)", which differ from Rec and Park's later page (construction beginning late 2028, opening early 2030).
